seo.title: Southeast Asia Semester Abroad | Pacific Discovery
seo.description: Thailand, Laos, Vietnam & Cambodia in 10 weeks: hill tribe and village homestays, elephant care, a Mekong slow boat, Halong Bay, Angkor Wat, community building projects and Krabi’s cliffs. Ages 17–22.

hero.eyebrow: Gap semester · Thailand, Laos, Vietnam & Cambodia
hero.headline: Four countries of Southeast Asia in one semester
hero.intro: Live with hill tribe families, care for elephants, slow-boat the Mekong into Laos, cruise Halong Bay, explore Angkor Wat and finish on Krabi’s limestone cliffs.
hero.imageAlt: Student rock climbing above a bay with longtail boats

items.title: Four countries, overland
items.body: Trains, vans, a two-day Mekong slow boat, an overnight cruise and a night train connect Thailand, Laos, Vietnam and Cambodia.

items.title: Homestays that go deep
items.body: Stay with hill tribe families in northern Thailand, Khmu and Hmong villages on a Laos trek, and a family in a Cambodian floating village.

items.title: Service across the region
items.body: Coffee nurseries in the hills, elephant care, village building in Mae Win, mangrove planting in Kampot and a building project with Volunteer Building Cambodia.

items.body: Comfortable guesthouses and modern hotels in towns and cities.

items.title: Homestays
items.body: Hill tribe families in northern Thailand, Khmu and Hmong villages on the Laos trek, and a floating village family in Cambodia, usually on mats with mosquito nets.

itinerary.heading: Week by week
itinerary.note: This is a guide to what you can expect to do on program. The order in which activities occur might vary. Itineraries are subject to change.

weeks.title: Bangkok to Sukhothai by bike
weeks.location: Bangkok → Ayutthaya → Sukhothai → Chiang Rai, Thailand
weeks.body:
You’ll meet your Program Instructors in Bangkok, then take the train to Ayutthaya, the ancient capital of Siam, and explore its temple ruins by mountain bike. A van takes us north to Sukhothai for a sunset bike tour of the historical park.

We visit Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat, the Thawee Folk Museum and Wat Chan Tawan Tok, hold our orientation, and spend a day at Si Satchanalai Historical Park, known for its traditional pottery. The week ends on the public bus to Chiang Rai.
weeks.imageAlt: Students waving from inside a tuk-tuk at night

weeks.title: Hill tribe homestay & Chiang Mai
weeks.body:
After a morning tour of Chiang Rai, we head into the hills to stay with hill tribe families. We cook dinner with our hosts, help build a coffee nursery and plant fruit trees, walk into the jungle to check local dams, and watch an evening dance performance.

Back in Chiang Rai we debrief, then take the bus to Chiang Mai for a walking tour of its big temple and markets, dinner at the night markets and a free day before heading to the elephants.

weeks.title: Elephants & village volunteering
weeks.location: Chiang Mai → Mae Win → Sansai, Thailand
weeks.body:
At Happy Elephant House we spend our days on elephant enrichment, clearing land and helping the local team with whatever is needed. The day is shaped by what the elephants need, and touching them is mostly not allowed. Each day also includes culture and temples.

Next we move to the countryside around Mae Win for two days of community volunteering, building alongside locals, before transferring to Sansai.
weeks.imageAlt: Students washing an elephant in a muddy river

weeks.title: Meditation & the Mekong into Laos
weeks.location: Sansai → Chiang Mai → Chiang Khong → Luang Prabang, Laos
weeks.body:
At a traditional meditation centre in Sansai, monks lead sessions in meditation and talks on the Buddhist traditions and philosophy that shape Thai culture. Back in Chiang Mai we have a private cooking class and another night market.

From Chiang Khong we cross the Friendship Bridge into Laos, then board a private slow boat for two days down the Mekong, overnighting in Pakbeng before arriving in Luang Prabang.
weeks.imageAlt: Group beside a river boat on a sandy riverbank

weeks.title: Trekking & village homestays in Laos
weeks.location: Luang Prabang → Nong Khiaw → Luang Prabang, Laos
weeks.body:
After a day exploring Luang Prabang, we set off on a four-day trek with Tiger Trails. A boat ride on the Nam Ou River takes us to Sob Khan for a picnic lunch, then we trek through karst mountains and jungle to Payong to meet our host families.

The next days take us to Na Luang, a Khmu and Hmong village, stopping at Tad Nang None waterfall, and through bamboo forests and over streams to the Hmong village of Patham, staying with families each night. We trek out to Vieng Kham and return to Luang Prabang, with time for Kuang Si waterfall before flying to Hanoi.
weeks.imageAlt: Two students jumping into the water from a boat

weeks.title: Hanoi, Halong Bay & going student-led
weeks.body:
A walking tour of Hanoi’s Old Quarter takes in Quan Thanh Temple and Cua Bac Gate. The next day we hike at the Perfume Pagoda and finish with a Hanoi street food walking tour.

Then we head to Halong Bay for an overnight cruise into Bai Tu Long Bay: kayaking at Cap La Island, a cooking demonstration, sunrise tai chi on deck and a visit to Thien Canh Son Cave. Back in Hanoi, the student-led section begins.
weeks.imageAlt: Students in aprons and straw hats at a cooking class

weeks.title: Student-led to Hoi An, then Saigon
weeks.body:
During the student-led section, you plan the route, budget and activities that take the group to Hoi An. There we meet our guide for dinner and take a boat to the Red Bridge Cooking School for a morning cooking class.

We fly to Saigon to tour the Cu Chi tunnels, have a free day, and then travel overland into Cambodia.
weeks.imageAlt: Students walking in front of an ornate gate

weeks.title: Phnom Penh, sun bears & mangroves
weeks.location: Phnom Penh → Kampot → Kep → Siem Reap, Cambodia
weeks.body:
In Phnom Penh we visit the Genocide Museum and Choeung Ek Killing Fields, then decompress on a sunset cruise and at the night markets. At a wildlife rescue centre we work alongside the animal care team as sun bear keepers.

In Kampot we paddleboard, plant mangroves and visit Champa Lodge gardens. From Kep we go island hopping and snorkeling, take a guided national park walk and an architecture tour, then ride the sleeper bus to Siem Reap for a countryside cycle tour through local villages and markets.
weeks.imageAlt: Student sitting at the front of a longtail boat between limestone islands

weeks.title: Angkor Wat, homestay & building
weeks.body:
We start early for a sunrise tour of Angkor Wat, then visit APOPO to see the landmine detection HeroRATs. A night in a floating village homestay follows, with a boat trip and an introduction to daily life on the water.

Back in Siem Reap we take a walking tour of a local pagoda and the royal gardens, eat at a street food market and watch the Phare Circus. Two days with Volunteer Building Cambodia on a community building project close out Cambodia before we fly to Bangkok for Muay Thai and the night train south.
weeks.imageAlt: Group sitting on the steps of an Angkor temple

weeks.title: From jungle to beach cliffs
weeks.location: Khao Sok → Ao Nang, Krabi, Thailand
weeks.body:
In Khao Sok National Park we visit the lake, go river tubing, start a day with yoga and head out on a night safari.

Then we transfer to Ao Nang in Krabi for a half day of rock climbing and a half day of kayaking. We finish with our program wrap and a final dinner before flying home from Krabi.
weeks.imageAlt: Student rock climbing above a bay with longtail boats

notes.title: Free time
notes.body: Each week there is some designated free time to catch up on email and laundry, rest and explore with others in the group.

notes.title: Phones & wifi
notes.body: We encourage flight mode so you stay present. Wifi is available where we stay in cities and towns.

notes.title: Fitness needed
notes.body: Medium activity level. Expect multi-day trekking in Laos, cycling, climbing and kayaking, and some physical work on volunteer projects.

items.title: Buddhism & meditation
items.body: Spend time at a traditional meditation centre where monks lead meditation and talk about the Buddhist traditions and philosophy that shape Thai culture.

items.title: Optional college credit
items.body: Earn college credit through the University of Montana. 529 education funds can be used to pay for your credits and your Pacific Discovery program tuition.

safety.heading: For parents: how we keep students safe

items.title: 24/7 Emergency Line
items.body: Parents, students and instructors can reach a real person at any hour. Every call is logged and passed to our on-call staff member by phone.

items.title: Wilderness First Aid & Live Risk Assessment
items.body: All our instructors hold Wilderness First Aid (WFA) certification and have extensive training in group leadership and risk management.

items.title: Accredited Safety Systems
items.body: Our safety systems are assessed and accredited by the Gap Year Association (USA), Year Out Group (UK) and OutdoorsMark (NZ). Students on Go Overseas voted us one of the top gap year providers for safety.

items.title: Insurance & Health
items.body: Comprehensive travel insurance is required, covering medical costs and emergency evacuation. Check vaccinations with your doctor, and pack a first-aid kit and any personal medication. Our instructors can't legally give students any medication.

faq.heading: Questions we get about this program

items.q: How fit do I need to be?
items.a: The program suits anyone of average fitness. You don't need experience with any of the activities, but be ready for a four-day trek in Laos, cycling, climbing and kayaking. Volunteer projects also involve some physical work.

Simple and welcoming. In the hill tribe village, on the Laos trek and in the floating village you’ll sleep on mats, usually with mosquito nets, and share meals with your hosts. A local guide is there to help.

items.q: What is the meditation centre like?
items.a: It's a traditional centre where monks lead the sessions. It's a chance to learn about the Buddhist traditions that shape Thai culture, so come ready to be respectful, quiet and curious.
In Vietnam the group plans its own route to Hoi An, managing the budget, transport, meals and activities, with your instructors there for guidance.

Tuition covers all in-country transport, accommodation, meals, and the activities and entry fees in the itinerary. It doesn't cover international flights, visas, travel insurance, spending money, optional college credit or optional activities.

items.q: How much spending money should I bring?
items.a: About $100 a week for snacks, laundry, personal shopping and optional activities. It varies from student to student.

items.q: Can I stay in touch with home?
items.a: Yes. We encourage keeping phones on flight mode so you stay present, and wifi is available where we stay in cities and towns. There will also be a photo album that students and instructors can upload photos and video to, so parents and caregivers can stay up to date.

items.q: Do I need a passport or visa?
items.a: Your passport must be valid for more than 6 months after the program ends. All the information you need in regard to visas will be available in your student portal.
